market_sizing.target_buyer: Owner of a small-to-mid solar installation business (1–25 staff: salespeople, designers, SAA-accredited installers, electricians). The CEC/SAA-accredited installer signs STC forms; the office admin (often the owner's partner) lodges them on REC Registry and chases STC-trader payments.
market_sizing.business_count_au: ~8,000+ SAA-accredited solar installers/designers (individuals). Installer-businesses are fewer — estimated 2,500–4,000 active retailer/installer companies in AU, plus a long tail of sole-trader sparkies who do occasional installs. The CEC Approved Solar Retailer scheme has ~150–200 firms; total installer-businesses well above that.
market_sizing.business_count_global: US: ~10,000+ residential solar contractors (NABCEP universe + state-licensed). UK: ~3,000 MCS-certified installers. Canada: ~1,500. The STC paperwork problem is AU-specific (Renewable Energy Target / SRES); global TAM for the same product is near zero — the data model generalises (jobs + photos + serial numbers + rebate paperwork) but the regulator/integration layer doesn't.
market_sizing.typical_size: Median 3–10 employees; revenue $500k–$5M. Battery-heavy and commercial installers tend to be larger (10–40 staff). Heavy churn at both ends — sole traders and rapid-growth retailers.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: OpenSolar: free (revenue from hardware/finance partners; OS 3.0 launched 2025 as 'free AI-powered solar OS'). Pylon: $4/project (Standard) or $10/project (Pro), CRM add-on $49/user/mo, eSignature $0.80/project. Aurora Solar: enterprise pricing, ~$200–500/user/mo (US-priced). Greenbot: STC trading + job management, pricing bundled with STC trade. GreenDeal: similar STC-trading-bundled model. ServiceM8/AroFlo/simPRO for the FSM piece. The big incumbent is essentially 'free + STC trader takes a clip' — a hard price ceiling.
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: $100–300/mo AUD for a pure ops/compliance tool is challenging because OpenSolar is free and Greenbot/GreenDeal monetise via STC trade margin. Realistic ARPU is achievable only if (a) bundled with STC trading where the take is the revenue, or (b) positioned as the compliance/audit-defence + serial-number ledger layer that the free tools don't do well.
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Self-serve + inside sales. Strong inbound from CER announcements, SAA partnership, and STC-trader partnerships. Cold outbound viable via SAA installer register.
pricing_reality.realistic_arpu_au: $120–250 AUD/mo for the SaaS-only line. If a transactional STC-clip is layered on, effective ARPU rises to $400–800 (3–5% of STC value at typical 6.6kW residential ~$2,500 STC value × 3–6 installs/mo).
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Very strong. STC trading clip (industry standard 3–5% of STC value); CER serial-number ledger compliance fees; battery rebate (Cheaper Home Batteries, effective 1 July 2025) paperwork; insurance / extended-warranty resale; finance origination (Brighte, Plenti, Humm). The embedded-fintech and embedded-rebate-trading angle is the real game — pure SaaS will struggle, but SaaS + transactional can easily 3× ARPU.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: 1) OpenSolar (Sydney, 2018; free; 25,000+ users in 160+ countries; OS 3.0 launched late 2025 with AI design + CRM). 2) Pylon (per-project pricing; design + CRM; rapidly growing). 3) Aurora Solar (US, enterprise; remote shading analysis). 4) Greenbot (AU; STC trading + job management; popular for the rebate workflow). 5) GreenDeal (AU; STC trading + compliance; competes head-on with Greenbot). 6) ServiceM8 / simPRO / AroFlo for the FSM/job side. 7) SolarPlus / SolarVue niche tools.
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: OpenSolar: ~7. Aurora Solar: ~12. Pylon: ~3 (young). Greenbot/GreenDeal: ~5–8. The category is younger than electrical/plumbing FSMs and the dominant player (OpenSolar) just relaunched in 2025, narrowing the UI-rot wedge.
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: GreenDeal Solar app review explicitly says 'Use GreenBot wherever possible' citing GreenDeal's job-history lookup and photo-quality issues — Greenbot vs GreenDeal complaint pattern is well-documented. Whirlpool thread 'Advice please — How to claim STC?' shows installer confusion on the lodgement process. Common complaints: (a) STC processing takes ~3 weeks without panel-validation, dropping to ~48 hours with validation — installers complain about cashflow waiting on STC payment; (b) serial-number mismatches and accreditation-detail errors stall claims; (c) the 2-installs-per-day cap (introduced as anti-fraud measure) restricts business model; (d) the CEC/SAA accreditation transition (handover completed 29 May 2024) caused months of registration confusion; (e) the SAA accreditation exam from 1 July 2025 has stranded some installers mid-renewal.
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: OpenSolar has raised multiple rounds (~$80M+ cumulative incl. AGL involvement). Pylon raised seed/Series A 2023–24. CEC handed over installer accreditation to SAA on 29 May 2024 (regulator-side consolidation, not M&A). Brighte (solar finance, AU) has expanded. ServiceTitan IPO Dec 2024 raises sector multiples. No notable AU pure-play STC-paperwork acquisitions in last 12 months.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: High. OpenSolar 3.0 (Oct/Nov 2025) is explicitly an 'AI-powered solar OS' — design, proposal and CRM with AI built-in. Pylon similarly leaning into AI design. New entrants will be AI-design-first by default; window for a non-AI entrant is closing fast. However, the compliance/rebate-paperwork niche is less AI-attacked than the design/proposal niche.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: Solar installers spend a disproportionate amount of admin time on STC paperwork: installer + designer compliance statements, electrical safety cert, panel serial numbers, geo-tagged photos with installer's face in shot, customer authorisation, and REC Registry submission with the correct CEC-approved module/inverter from the (changing!) approved-product list. The CER now mandates serial-number-level traceability (CER solar panel ledger initiative) and limits installers to 2 installations/day as fraud control. The CEC was provided with evidence of installers signing false declarations, leading to a 'compliance is responsibility, not choice' campaign. Audit risk is real — false declarations contravene the Renewable Energy (Electricity) Act 2000 and trigger fraud prosecutions. Existing free tools (OpenSolar) do design and proposal beautifully but compliance/audit-defence is weaker; STC traders (Greenbot, GreenDeal) take a clip but don't fully solve the photo-evidence + serial-ledger + audit-trail workflow.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: 1) Direct REC Registry bulk-upload integration + CER serial-number ledger compliance. 2) SAA partnership for installer verification + CPD logging (100 CPD points/12 months required). 3) Photo-evidence ML (face detection of installer on site, EXIF/geo verification, serial-number OCR). 4) STC trading partnerships (clip-of-trade revenue). 5) Battery-rebate (Cheaper Home Batteries 1 Jul 2025) paperwork rule engine. Moat depth: medium — OpenSolar can match the design/CRM piece but is unlikely to want the regulated compliance/serial-ledger headache; that's the wedge.
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: REC Registry (CER) bulk upload; CER approved-products list (PV modules, batteries, inverters — refreshed 6 May 2026); SAA accreditation register; STC traders (Demand Manager, Greenbank, Greenbot, GreenDeal); state DNSP grid-connection portals (Ausgrid, Endeavour, Essential, AusNet, SAPN, etc.); Xero/MYOB; Brighte/Plenti/Humm for finance; OpenSolar/Pylon API (sidecar play); CEC Approved Retailer scheme for retailer-side firms.
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: Moderate. OpenSolar is free and increasingly the de-facto design tool — its CRM expansion (OS 3.0) is eating side-car opportunities. Side-car positioning as 'the compliance/audit layer next to OpenSolar' is the safer wedge; rip-and-replace OpenSolar is hard at price zero.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: Very high. CER scheme + SAA accreditation + state DNSP rules + state-level battery rebate + state electrical licence + AS/NZS 5033 (PV install) + AS/NZS 4777 (inverter) + AS/NZS 5139 (battery). Photo-evidence rules from CER are detailed (time/date metadata, geolocation, installer's face, serial number visible on product). The 2-installs-per-day cap and the CER ledger require audit-grade traceability.
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: 1 July 2025: Federal Cheaper Home Batteries Program (STC discount extended to batteries) launched — new SKU of paperwork for installers, new battery STC calc, new CER approved-products list for batteries. 28 June 2025: SAA Accreditation Exam replaces case study for all new applicants. May 2026: New CER Approved PV Modules / Batteries / Inverters lists become applicable for REC Registry bulk upload. CER serial-number ledger initiative is actively being built (per SolarQuotes coverage). CEC compliance crackdown post-false-declaration evidence (continues through 2025–26). State-level battery rebates (NSW Peak Demand Reduction Scheme; VIC Solar Homes battery loan changes) creating more rebate paperwork. The federal battery scheme + CER ledger + SAA exam together are a once-a-decade churn event for the industry.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: High. Need to understand DC vs AC coupling, panel/inverter/battery matching, AS/NZS standards, DNSP application flow (pre-approval vs post-install notification varies by state), STC create-vs-sell pricing dynamics, and audit-survival best practice. Acquirable by an outsider in 4–6 months with a SAA-accredited installer advisor.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 6–9 months solo. Slightly heavier than electrical because the photo-evidence + serial-number + REC Registry stack is non-trivial. STC-only MVP (job + photos + serial-OCR + REC Registry submit) is feasible in 5 months. Audit-defence + battery rebate paperwork adds 2–3 months.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: 1) Serial-number OCR from on-site photos at variable angles/lighting (ML inference cost). 2) REC Registry API/bulk-upload reliability and format changes (CER moves the approved-products list periodically, schedule for 6 May 2026 cited). 3) DNSP grid-connection portals — every distribution network has its own form/API (8+ DNSPs in AU). 4) Audit-trail immutability for fraud-prosecution-grade evidence. 5) Battery-rebate calc as battery-STC interacts with system size and existing solar.
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: High — DNSP application + state battery rebate + state electrical licence differ by state. STC scheme is federal so the core rebate engine is one rule engine, but the grid-connection + state-rebate layer is 8 DNSPs.
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: Not legally mandated but expected given CER serial ledger may push for AU-hosted audit data; AU Supabase region recommended.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: 1) SEO: 'CER serial number ledger', 'battery STC calculator', 'SAA accreditation exam software', 'solar audit defence Australia'. 2) SAA partnership / CPD-points-bearing training. 3) STC-trader co-marketing (Demand Manager, Greenbank). 4) Smart Energy Council, Clean Energy Council membership channels. 5) Solar industry FB groups (CEC Accredited Installers, Solar Installers Australia). 6) SolarQuotes blog/forum, Solar Choice, Whirlpool. 7) Trade shows: Smart Energy Conference (April annually, Sydney), All-Energy Australia (Oct annually, Melbourne) — both >5k attendees, exhibit cost a stretch above $10k for premium booths but small booth/sponsor packs under $10k exist. 8) Cold outbound — SAA installer register is public.
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: ~4–5: Smart Energy Council (peak), Clean Energy Council (broader renewables), Solar Energy Industries Association of Australia (smaller), Master Electricians Australia (gas adjacency), state-level installer groups.
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: ~5: Solar Quotes Blog (largest AU solar audience), SolarChoice, EcoGeneration, PV Magazine Australia, Renew Economy. Sponsorship slots are accessible but more competitive than electrical.
distribution_difficulty.industry_facebook_group_size: Estimated 15–35k combined members across the top AU solar-installer FB groups. Smaller than electrical but more digitally engaged.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: 2–3 major: Smart Energy Conference (Sydney, April), All-Energy Australia (Melbourne, October), state-level industry days. Booth cost frequently exceeds $10k for premium spots; sponsor/sub-booth options under $10k exist.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: High. SAA installer register is publicly searchable with state filter; CEC Approved Retailer list is published. Personal mobile + business email coverage is high.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Solar installer industry is software-friendly (already adopted OpenSolar/Pylon/Greenbot at scale). Outsider founder is fine if endorsed by SAA, a major STC trader, or a respected installer. The bigger trust hurdle is the heavy fraud-prosecution environment — buyers want a vendor who clearly understands CER audit rules.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: Moderate. Free-tier in exchange for case study works; expect 6–10 weeks for first 5 reference customers given installer attention is split across the active battery-rebate gold rush.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Moderate–high. SolarQuotes, Solar Choice, OpenSolar, Pylon all rank heavily for category keywords. The compliance/audit/CER-ledger sub-niche is much less crowded and rankable.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: Yes — REC Registry is a hard gatekeeper (every STC must be lodged there). SAA accreditation register access is needed. DNSP grid-connection APIs are gatekept by each distribution network. CER serial-number ledger, once mandated, will be a single high-stakes integration. This is the highest gatekeeper-density of the three options.

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: 25–35%. Reusable: multi-tenant auth + RLS, customer/job entities, file/photo storage, supplier/manufacturer (panel/inverter/battery brands) entity, part-number/serial-number model (panels have serial numbers — this maps directly to Manuva's inventory item model), Xero integration, activity_log. Surprisingly good fit because serial-number tracking and supplier-managed part lists are core to both.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: Auth, tenant RLS, file upload + signed URLs, supplier/part schema, activity_log, Xero OAuth, Next.js App Router, design tokens. Photo-evidence storage patterns from Manuva goods-inwards transfer.
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: Low–moderate. Manuva targets manufacturers; some overlap with pre-fab solar mounting/inverter assembly shops. Solar installers themselves are field-service, not factory.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Moderate. The serial-number + approved-product-list + supplier model has stronger conceptual overlap with Manuva than electrical or plumbing compliance.
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 9–15 months. OpenSolar/Pylon adding AI-design fast; the compliance/audit-defence/serial-ledger niche is harder to copy because it requires REC Registry trust and CER-ledger compliance, but a well-funded competitor could match within ~12 months.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Mixed. SMS + photo storage are normal. Real cost drivers: (a) serial-number OCR ML inference (~$0.05–0.20/photo at scale × ~25 photos/install × ~10 installs/mo = $12–50/customer/mo — could erode margin meaningfully). (b) Audit-evidence cold storage. (c) Possibly per-STC fees if a transactional model is layered on. Pure SaaS gross margin ~70–78% (lower than electrical/plumbing). If the model is SaaS + STC-trading clip, effective revenue per customer rises sharply and margin is dominated by STC-trader payout terms.
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Limited. Most solar installers are single-warehouse, multi-truck. Per-tech / per-installer seat expansion is the natural axis.
unit_economics.churn_risk: High. Solar installer churn is notoriously high — project-based, rebate-cycle-driven, frequent owner exits. Industry baseline 15–25%/yr is realistic. STC-trading lock-in (if model includes it) drops churn meaningfully but creates concentration risk in the STC market price.
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: At $200 ARPU AUD pure SaaS: ~420 customers for $1M ARR. With STC clip layered on (effective ~$600 blended): ~140 customers. Achievable from a pool of 2,500–4,000 installer-businesses at 3–5% adoption, especially with SAA or STC-trader partnership.
